title: Delhi Consumer Commission Holds Union Bank Liable for Jewellery Missing From a Surrendered Locker
court: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
case_name: Monica Marwah v. Union Bank of India
card_summary: Monica Marwah and her late father-in-law held a joint locker at Union Bank's Naraina Vihar branch from 1998. When she sought access in 2018, the bank said it was already surrendered years earlier but produced no letter from her for its closure. The Commission held the bank had not proved valid surrender or return of the jewellery, worth Rs 47 lakh, and ordered that sum paid with 6% interest from September 2018.
card_tip: A bank that closes a joint locker without a signed request or acknowledgment from every holder on record stays exposed to the full value of its contents years later.
verification_notes: Case number CC/249/2019, branch (Naraina Vihar), locker start date (1998), the bank's conflicting surrender dates, the finding of deficiency, the Rs 47 lakh figure and 6% interest from September 2018, and the order date (27 Oct 2026) confirmed across Bar and Bench and The 420. Outlook Money's larger Rs 50.5 lakh total (adding compensation and costs) is not corroborated by the other two reports, so only the Rs 47 lakh principal and interest are stated here.
